advice: Propose a distinct one-level Strassen variant that removes the separate full-output zeroing pass. Keep the same three dense 256×256 FP32 work buffers, seven approved products, and helper mapping: zeroed 22-slot parameters with [4]=right, [10]=left, [16]=dense product. Pack each 512-stride parent quadrant into dense operands before calling the helper. On P1, store its values to C11 and C22 as their initial values. On P2, store C21 and subtract from C22. On P3, store C12 and add to C22. Apply the remaining contributions in order: P4 adds to C11 and C21; P5 subtracts from C11 and adds to C12; P6 adds to C22; P7 adds to C11. This preserves C11=P1+P4−P5+P7, C12=P3+P5, C21=P2+P4, and C22=P1−P2+P3+P6 while avoiding the separate zero-fill and first read-modify-write for each output element. Keep all packing, allocation, helper calls, accumulation, and frees inside gemm. Other sizes and allocation failure use the unchanged general fallback. This is a proposal, not a measured speedup.
risks: The change must initialize every C element exactly once before later accumulation; incorrect first-store handling can leave outputs unwritten or use stale C. The three-buffer Strassen wrapper was rejected after losing all ten measured pairs, so this smaller store-traffic change may not address its main costs. FP32 product sums and accumulation order retain the same cancellation and scale-sensitive accuracy risks. Before timing, check all seven operand equations and signs, dense helper mapping, public shapes and tails, n<=0, allocation failure, full overwrite, guards, finite results, unchanged inputs, and the existing 0.002 tolerance including deterministic cancellation and scale-separated cases. If correct, use the unchanged ten validations, ten alternating paired controls, promotion gate, and held-out check.
